inputs.text: They announced a ceasefire five months ago, yet airstrikes are still killing civilians and daily life in Gaza remains under drones, gunfire, shelling, and fire directed at fishermen. That contradiction is the point: the ceasefire label gives powerful institutions a story of progress while the reality on the ground keeps getting more brutal. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says the drones “never stop buzzing overhead.” This looks less like peace and more like a managed narrative designed to make ongoing destruction easier to ignore.
